overall_safety_summary: The scene is generally organized, but safety risks are present due to a protruding pan handle on the left and improper hand positioning close to the knife blade while chopping.

hazards.description: A metal pan handle is protruding outward over the edge of the stove or counter on the left side.
hazards.explanation: This creates a risk of accidentally bumping into the handle, which could cause the pan to fall or spill its contents.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults with reduced peripheral vision or mobility limitations are at a higher risk of bumping into protruding objects.
hazards.recommended_action: Turn the pan handle inward so it does not extend past the edge of the counter or stove.

hazards.description: The person's left hand is resting very close to the active cutting area without using a protective claw grip.
hazards.explanation: Improper hand placement increases the risk of accidental cuts or slips of the knife blade.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults may experience reduced hand stability or slower reflexes, making safe knife techniques especially critical to prevent injuries.
hazards.recommended_action: Curl the fingers of the non-dominant hand inward into a claw grip to keep them safe from the knife blade.

uncertainties: It is unclear whether the pan on the left is hot or contains liquid.
It is uncertain if the cutting board has a non-slip backing or mat underneath to prevent sliding.
